rationale: Codebase-pin lens, all five assignments verified empirically at commit 68ede240. (1) Tests real and green: full `go test -short ./...` exits 0 (40 ok packages, no FAIL); all 12 new bead-5 tests (verb_output_test.go, cwdsafety_test.go additions) run verbosely and PASS, none skipped. (2) AC-14's classification is genuinely total and mechanized, probed in BOTH directions in a /tmp copy (deleted after): registering an unclassified dummy cobra command went RED naming 'mindspec probe-dummy'; unregistering an allowlisted command (bench) went RED as a stale entry. The forward wantRows assertion additionally pins the nine R2.1 verbs by name, so dropping a mutating row is also red. (3) The execution drives are over real production wiring, not mocks-of-mocks: spec approve drives the real approveSpecRunE whose last act is the REAL emitInstruct — I patched a /tmp copy to dump the captured output and confirmed the real Plan Mode template ('## MindSpec Lifecycle') renders AFTER the 'approved' result line (ordering assertion empirically non-vacuous; captureStdout genuinely swaps os.Stdout so emitInstruct's direct writes are captured). completeTail's two cwdsafety tests drive the real extracted production tail: the indeterminate branch goes through the real instruct.RenderIndeterminate (real template render, ADR-0035 'recovery: mindspec doctor' asserted as the literal last line) and t.Fatals if instructFn is ever called; the success branch asserts the indeterminate marker's ABSENCE plus instructFn invocation, closing the vacuous-pass hole round-2 G11 named. Seams sit only at the bd/executor leaves (stubApproveBeadsForVerbTest mirrors internal/harness's proven stateful epic-registry stub; newExecutorFn swaps only the worktree-creating executor). (4) Pin-inventory claim verified at diff level: agreement_table_test.go's change is a single comment block (the G3.1 disclosure updated to the true remaining reason — package-import boundary, not draft-unawareness); lifecycle-modes.md changes only row 1's Notes prose; no agreement-table cell MODE changed anywhere, and the bead-4 structural pins are part of the green suite. (5) The ratchet census bump 14→15 is honest: indeterminate.md contains exactly one interpolation, {{termsafe .IndeterminateReason}}, and its classification as classTermsafeText is correct — the reason wraps bd/git error chains that can embed agent-writable IDs/paths, so termsafe routing is the right class (same as idle.md's termsafe text). Disclosure D holds from this lens: next/impl adopt remain red-if-removed via wantRows + the stale-entry check I probed.

findings.title: resultBeforeGuidance passes when no guidance marker appears at all
findings.detail: cmd/mindspec/verb_output_test.go's resultBeforeGuidance only fails when a marker precedes the result; for the emitInstruct-tailed driven verbs (spec create/approve, plan approve) it does not assert that at least one marker is PRESENT, so a future regression that silently suppresses the tail entirely (e.g. the worktree-redirect path firing, which prints '## Worktree Redirect' — not one of mindspecGuidanceMarkers) would still pass the ordering check. Today it is empirically non-vacuous (I confirmed the real Plan Mode template renders in the spec-approve drive, and every instruct template carries at least one marker), and a tail RENDER error would fail the RunE. Suggested hardening for a later bead, not this one: for tailed verbs, require >=1 marker present after the result index.

findings.title: complete/impl approve rows are tail-level drives; the RunE-to-tail hop is inspection-verified only
findings.detail: TestVerbOutput_Complete and TestVerbOutput_ImplApprove drive the real production completeTail/implApproveTail with hand-built Results and a stub instructFn supplying the marker. The tails ARE the production ordering authority (completeCmd.RunE cmd/mindspec/complete.go:146 passes the Run result straight to completeTail with no other stdout writes on success), so this satisfies the claimed 'RunE/tail wiring' and matches the established spec-092 R3-2 extraction pattern; noting for the record that the RunE->tail hop itself is covered by code inspection rather than a test.
